messages:
sahil: Heads up — after last night's kernel + NV driver push ~10 nodes in us-west-2 show missing MIG profiles and GPU UUIDs flipped. Cluster MIG capacity down ~18%.
infra-bot: deploy-batch completed: kernel-rebase-2024-11-05 on usw2-gpu fleet at 03:22 UTC :white_check_mark:
anya: seeing the same. k8s autoscaler triggered and a bunch of g4-like pods are Pending because no matching MIG profiles exist for the limits.
marc: can you paste `nvidia-smi -L` and `nvidia-smi mig -lgci` from an affected host? helps narrow nvml vs runtime issue.
sahil: here from usw2-gpu-012:
```
$ nvidia-smi -L
GPU 0: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-REPLACED-1234)
GPU 1: NVIDIA A100-SXM4-80GB (UUID: GPU-REPLACED-5678)

$ nvidia-smi mig -L
No MIG devices found.
```
lucy: weird — NVML is reporting the UUID as something that looks like a PCI re-assignment string on some hosts. dmesg shows a bunch of device_rescan/driver probe around boot.
anya: is this the same drift we saw months ago? that was a udev/udevrace with early driver init. but we did driver+kernel together this time so could be a timing/reg ordering issue.
marc: potential theory: driver binds before the vfio/udev mapping finishes -> kernel sees different PCI slot ordering so NVML generates new UUIDs. check `dmesg | grep -i nvrm` and `udevadm info`.
sahil: dmesg snippet from the node:
```
[   12.345678] NVRM: GPU UUID: GPU-abcdef12 changed from GPU-0000 to GPU-1111
[   12.346789] nvidia: probe of 0000:81:00.0 failed with error -5
[   12.347000] nvidia: NVML: failed to initialize MIG: No MIG devices found
```
lucy: starting a canary reprovision on usw2-gpu-031 — re-run MIG config scripts manually and attempt `nvidia-smi mig -cgi` to re-create profiles. if that doesn't work we'll revert.
ops-bot: escalation: paging @sre-oncall — high-impact infra regression detected (MIG capacity loss).
marc: if rollback necessary prefer kernel rollback first (we kept previous kernel in grub). driver reinstall after that. but also inspect AMI changes — did the new image include a different device-tree/PCI patch?
anya: cost note: autoscaler spun up a few non-GPU nodes and some workloads drained to cheaper instances but we saw a ~2.3% increase in spot spend last 6h. I'll add this to the incident cost tracker.
sahil: tagged affected hosts in the incident: usw2-gpu-012, 013, 014, 027, 031. I'll open a postmortem if the canary fails.
lucy: :thumbsup: will try udev ordering fix (add systemd service to delay nvidia module load until pci-rescan completes) and report back in ~20m.
infra-bot: Incident created: INC-20241105-82 — linked to this thread.
